name: KidsCheckin.com
shortDescription: A newer children’s ministry check-in service with free and paid daily check-in limits, unlimited devices, labels and CSV exports.
suitableContexts: Churches wanting a low-cost check-in pilot
Teams comfortable evaluating an early-access supplier

pricing.summary: KidsCheckin.com publishes a free plan for 30 daily check-ins, then $15, $29 and $49 monthly plans for 100, 500 and unlimited daily check-ins. It states no contracts, a 30-day money-back guarantee and free onboarding.

editorial.assessment: KidsCheckin.com has transparent entry pricing and a free tier, but it describes itself as opening early access to additional churches. It should be piloted carefully, with particular attention to reliability, data handling, printer compatibility and support before it is used for live child data.
bestFor: Small churches testing a dedicated check-in tool
Teams willing to assess a newer product cautiously
strengths: Free tier and clear daily-check-in price bands
Unlimited devices and CSV export are published
limitations: Only Dymo LabelWriter support is stated on the reviewed page

longForm.verdict: KidsCheckin.com is attractive for a low-cost pilot, but early-access software should not be the sole safeguarding control at a busy children’s ministry until the church has tested it thoroughly.

decisionLens.heading: Pilot with non-sensitive test data first.
decisionLens.text: A free plan makes evaluation easy, but the church needs evidence that printing, collection flow, exports and support work in its own environment. Keep existing procedures and fallback records in place during the pilot.

sections.heading: Affordable early-access check-in
sections.question: Can it meet the church’s real Sunday reliability standard?
paragraphs: KidsCheckin.com lists a free plan and paid daily check-in limits, unlimited devices, label printing, attendance and CSV export. It says it is opening early access to more churches.

Use dummy records during setup and test the approved printer, connection and recovery process. Only progress to live data when the safeguarding lead and children’s team are satisfied with privacy, access and collection arrangements.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on KidsCheckin.com’s official product and pricing page.
themes: The free plan lowers the cost of a controlled pilot.
Early-access status makes operational testing particularly important.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier claims are not an independent assessment of safety, reliability or UK data-protection suitability.

faq.question: Is KidsCheckin.com free?
faq.answer: Yes. The supplier lists a $0 plan for up to 30 daily check-ins.

faq.question: How much do paid plans cost?
faq.answer: Published plans are $15, $29 and $49 per month for up to 100, 500 and unlimited daily check-ins.

faq.question: Does it support all label printers?
faq.answer: Not confirmed. The reviewed page specifically states support for Dymo LabelWriter printers; ask about your required hardware.
